name: Folly-Desolate
geological_features: Eroded remnants of what were once mountain ranges
Dry lake beds containing mineral salt deposits
Wind-polished bedrock exposure across the equator
specific_features: Three separate failed colony foundations, each built atop the ruins of the previous attempt
description: Folly-Desolate is a barren world that looks as though it was once something more. Eroded mountain stumps line the horizon, dry lake beds spread like white scars across the lowlands, and the equatorial bedrock has been polished by wind into smooth planes that reflect the sky with a dull sheen. Everything here speaks of loss, of water and atmosphere and possibility that departed long ago.

The thin atmosphere carries enough dust to create faint, colorless hazes at dawn and dusk, but otherwise the world is stark and unforgiving. There is a quietness here that goes beyond silence, the absence not just of sound but of potential, as though the planet has exhausted every possibility it once held.

Three separate colonial expeditions chose Folly-Desolate as their new home over the course of four centuries, each one building atop the ruins of the previous attempt. The first failed to toxic mineral contamination of their water recyclers. The second succumbed to a structural failure during a dust storm. The third simply left, their departure logs recording only that the world was not what they had hoped.

The layered ruins form an accidental archaeological record of declining ambition, each foundation smaller and more modest than the one below it. Folly-Desolate's resources are adequate but uninspiring, its conditions survivable but punishing, and its history a three-part lesson in the gap between what survey data promises and what reality delivers.
